This notebook compares Connecticut Light and Power's 2025 average-customer hourly
loads with the weighted-average grid consumption CAIRO bills for the same
Eversource buildings.

The company file is an Excel workbook of class-average loads, one column each for
Rate 1, Rate 5, and Rate 7. We use 2025 only. Rate 1 is compared with homes whose
baseline heating type is natural gas, delivered fuel, or other. Rate 5 is compared
with electric-resistance and heat-pump homes. Rate 7 is not used.

Grid consumption is `grid_cons_kwh` from the `default_precalc` delivery run. Each
ResStock profile is the sample-weighted mean across buildings in that group. The
company series is interval-ending Eastern Standard Time with no daylight-saving
skip, so we shift it back one hour and line the two series up by hour of the year.
ResStock is an AMY weather year, not calendar 2025, so the join is by position.

A positive difference means the company's average customer uses more electricity
in that hour than the ResStock average home. Percent difference divides that gap
by the ResStock value.

## Company hourly loads

The workbook is an uploaded Excel file, so the Sheets API will not open it. We
download the bytes through Drive and read the `2025 ` tab. Row 6 holds the
company's own annual totals. Hourly values start at row 10, in kW for the hour
ending at the timestamp, which equals kWh for that hour.

```{python}
#| label: download-company-workbook

def download_company_workbook(path: Path) -> Path:
    """Cache the class-load workbook locally. Drive hosts it as xlsx, not a Sheet."""
    if path.exists():
        return path
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    gc, _ = get_gspread_client()
    session = AuthorizedSession(gc.http_client.auth)
    resp = session.get(
        f"https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{SHEET_ID}",
        params={"alt": "media"},
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    path.write_bytes(resp.content)
    return path


xlsx_path = download_company_workbook(CACHE_XLSX)
print(f"Workbook: {xlsx_path} ({xlsx_path.stat().st_size:,} bytes)")
```

```{python}
#| label: load-company-2025

def load_company_2025(path: Path) -> tuple[pl.DataFrame, dict[str, float]]:
    """Hour-beginning 2025 loads for Rate 1 and Rate 5, plus stated annual totals."""
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    ws = wb[SHEET_YEAR]
    stated: dict[str, float] = {}
    records: list[dict[str, datetime | float]] = []
    for i, row in enumerate(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True), start=1):
        if i == 6 and row[0] == "Total Usage":
            stated = {"rate_1": float(row[1]), "rate_5": float(row[2])}
        if i >= 10 and row[0] is not None:
            records.append(
                {
                    "interval_ending": row[0],
                    "rate_1_kw": float(row[1]),
                    "rate_5_kw": float(row[2]),
                }
            )
    wb.close()
    if len(records) != N_HOURS:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected {N_HOURS} hourly rows, found {len(records)}")
    hourly = (
        pl.DataFrame(records)
        .with_columns((pl.col("interval_ending") - pl.duration(hours=1)).alias("timestamp"))
        .with_row_index("hour_index")
        .select("hour_index", "timestamp", "rate_1_kw", "rate_5_kw")
    )
    return hourly, stated


company_hourly, stated_annual = load_company_2025(xlsx_path)
print("Stated annual kWh:", stated_annual)
print(
    f"Hour-beginning span: {company_hourly['timestamp'].min()} → {company_hourly['timestamp'].max()}"
)
company_hourly.head(3)
```

The Rate 1 and Rate 5 columns should sum to the Total Usage row on the sheet.

```{python}
#| label: check-company-annual

company_annual = {
    "rate_1": float(company_hourly["rate_1_kw"].sum()),
    "rate_5": float(company_hourly["rate_5_kw"].sum()),
}
for rate, total in company_annual.items():
    stated = stated_annual[rate]
    gap = total - stated
    print(f"{rate}: summed hourly {total:,.2f} kWh, sheet total {stated:,.2f}, gap {gap:+.4f}")
    if abs(gap) > 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{rate} hourly sum differs from the sheet total by {gap:.2f} kWh")
```

## ResStock populations

Heating type comes from the `default_precalc` master bills, the same classification
used for the monthly median comparison. Weights are ResStock sample weights.

```{python}
#| label: load-populations

meta = (
    load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, SEGMENT)
    .filter((pl.col("month") == "Annual") & (pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY))
    .select(
        "bldg_id",
        "weight",
        pl.col("postprocess_group.heating_type_v2").alias("heating_type_v2"),
    )
    .collect()
)

pop_rate_1 = meta.filter(pl.col("heating_type_v2").is_in(RATE_1_HEATING))
pop_rate_5 = meta.filter(pl.col("heating_type_v2").is_in(RATE_5_HEATING))

for label, pop in [("Rate 1 (gas, delivered fuel, other)", pop_rate_1), ("Rate 5 (electric heat)", pop_rate_5)]:
    print(
        f"{label}: {pop.height:,} buildings, {float(pop['weight'].sum()):,.0f} weighted households"
    )
    print(pop.group_by("heating_type_v2").agg(n=pl.len(), weight=pl.col("weight").sum()).sort("heating_type_v2"))
```

`billing_kwh_8760.parquet` on the delivery run is the grid consumption CAIRO uses
for bills. We take the weighted mean of `grid_cons_kwh` at each timestamp.

```{python}
#| label: resstock-hourly-profiles

kwh_8760 = load_billing_kwh_8760(STATE, UTILITY, BATCH, SEGMENT)

rs_rate_1 = weighted_avg_hourly(
    kwh_8760, pop_rate_1["bldg_id"].to_list(), pop_rate_1.select("bldg_id", "weight")
).with_row_index("hour_index").rename({"kwh": "resstock_kwh"})
rs_rate_5 = weighted_avg_hourly(
    kwh_8760, pop_rate_5["bldg_id"].to_list(), pop_rate_5.select("bldg_id", "weight")
).with_row_index("hour_index").rename({"kwh": "resstock_kwh"})

for label, profile in [("Rate 1", rs_rate_1), ("Rate 5", rs_rate_5)]:
    if profile.height != N_HOURS:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} ResStock profile has {profile.height} hours, expected {N_HOURS}")
    print(f"{label} ResStock annual kWh: {float(profile['resstock_kwh'].sum()):,.1f}")
```

## Hourly difference

`delta_kwh` is the company value minus ResStock. `pct_diff` divides that gap by
the ResStock hour.

```{python}
#| label: hourly-delta

def hourly_comparison(company: pl.DataFrame, company_col: str, resstock: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Align a company rate column to a ResStock profile by hour-of-year index."""
    joined = company.select("hour_index", "timestamp", pl.col(company_col).alias("company_kwh")).join(
        resstock.select("hour_index", "resstock_kwh"),
        on="hour_index",
        how="inner",
    )
    if joined.height != N_HOURS:
        raise ValueError(f"Joined profile has {joined.height} hours, expected {N_HOURS}")
    return joined.with_columns(
        (pl.col("company_kwh") - pl.col("resstock_kwh")).alias("delta_kwh"),
    ).with_columns(
        (pl.col("delta_kwh") / pl.col("resstock_kwh")).alias("pct_diff"),
    )


hourly_rate_1 = hourly_comparison(company_hourly, "rate_1_kw", rs_rate_1)
hourly_rate_5 = hourly_comparison(company_hourly, "rate_5_kw", rs_rate_5)

def headline(label: str, hourly: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
    annual_delta = float(hourly["delta_kwh"].sum())
    mae = float(hourly["delta_kwh"].abs().mean())
    peak = hourly.sort(pl.col("delta_kwh").abs(), descending=True).row(0, named=True)
    print(
        f"{label}: annual delta {annual_delta:+,.0f} kWh, "
        f"mean absolute hourly delta {mae:.3f} kWh, "
        f"largest gap {peak['delta_kwh']:+.3f} kWh "
        f"({peak['pct_diff']:+.1%}) at {peak['timestamp']}"
    )


headline("Rate 1", hourly_rate_1)
headline("Rate 5", hourly_rate_5)
hourly_rate_1.head(3)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hourly-delta
#| fig-cap: "Hourly difference between Eversource's 2025 class-average customer and the ResStock weighted-average home. Positive values mean the company customer uses more electricity that hour."

plot_df = pl.concat(
    [
        hourly_rate_1.select("timestamp", "delta_kwh", pl.lit("Rate 1").alias("comparison")),
        hourly_rate_5.select("timestamp", "delta_kwh", pl.lit("Rate 5").alias("comparison")),
    ]
).with_columns(pl.col("comparison").cast(pl.Enum(["Rate 1", "Rate 5"])))

(
    ggplot(plot_df, aes("timestamp", "delta_kwh"))
    + geom_hline(yintercept=0, color=SB_COLORS["midnight_text"], size=0.4)
    + geom_line(color=SB_COLORS["sky"], size=0.3)
    + facet_wrap("comparison", ncol=1)
    + scale_x_datetime(date_breaks="2 months", date_labels="%b")
    + labs(
        title="Company average customer minus ResStock average home",
        x="",
        y="kWh",
    )
    + theme_switchbox()
    + theme(figure_size=(10.5, 7))
)
```

## Monthly summary

Each month sums the hourly kWh first. The percent difference is the gap between
those monthly totals divided by the ResStock monthly total, not the average of
the hourly percents. The annual row is the same calculation over all 8,760 hours.

```{python}
#| label: monthly-summary

_month_labels = {i + 1: name for i, name in enumerate(MONTH_ORDER)}
_month_labels[13] = "Annual"
_month_order = [*MONTH_ORDER, "Annual"]


def monthly_summary(hourly: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Company, ResStock, kWh gap, and percent difference by month, plus annual."""
    by_month = (
        hourly.group_by(pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("month_num"))
        .agg(pl.col("company_kwh").sum(), pl.col("resstock_kwh").sum())
        .with_columns(pl.col("month_num").cast(pl.Int32))
        .sort("month_num")
    )
    annual = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "month_num": pl.Series([13], dtype=pl.Int32),
            "company_kwh": [float(by_month["company_kwh"].sum())],
            "resstock_kwh": [float(by_month["resstock_kwh"].sum())],
        }
    )
    return (
        pl.concat([by_month, annual])
        .with_columns((pl.col("company_kwh") - pl.col("resstock_kwh")).alias("delta_kwh"))
        .with_columns((pl.col("delta_kwh") / pl.col("resstock_kwh")).alias("pct_diff"))
        .with_columns(pl.col("month_num").replace_strict(_month_labels).alias("month"))
        .with_columns(pl.col("month").cast(pl.Enum(_month_order)))
        .sort("month")
        .select("month", "company_kwh", "resstock_kwh", "delta_kwh", "pct_diff")
    )


monthly_rate_1 = monthly_summary(hourly_rate_1)
monthly_rate_5 = monthly_summary(hourly_rate_5)


def show_monthly(title: str, monthly: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
    table = (
        GT(monthly, rowname_col="month")
        .tab_header(title=title)
        .fmt_number(columns=["company_kwh", "resstock_kwh", "delta_kwh"], decimals=0)
        .fmt_percent(columns=["pct_diff"], decimals=1)
        .cols_label(
            company_kwh="Company kWh",
            resstock_kwh="ResStock kWh",
            delta_kwh="Difference",
            pct_diff="Percent difference",
        )
        .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
    )
    display_gt(table)


show_monthly("Rate 1 vs gas, delivered-fuel, and other homes", monthly_rate_1)
show_monthly("Rate 5 vs electric-resistance and heat-pump homes", monthly_rate_5)
```
